meta.canon_status_description: Post-Fate of the Jedi (47 ABY) Legends continuity. Legacy comics did not happen. The One Sith on Korriban remain in patient pre-emergence under Darth Krayt. All other post-FOTJ continuity is preserved, including Crucible (45 ABY): Luke/Leia/Han had a Mortis-adjacent metaphysical encounter and stepped back from active galactic crisis-management work; the Jedi Order relocated permanently from Coruscant to Shedu Maad (Hapes Cluster) at the end of FOTJ (44 ABY); Saba Sebatyne assumed the Grand Master role when Luke stepped down.
meta.era: Legacy Era, post-Fate of the Jedi, 47 ABY
meta.tone_description: Postwar conspiracy thriller register. Cinematic clarity, adventure momentum, lived-in technology, dry humor, mythic Force awe when earned. Commercial readability beats literary flourish. Reader pleasure before theme — the deeper themes (restraint can cost lives, Jacen's crisis logic can save lives, forbidden knowledge may be necessary to heal or protect) settle in as aftertaste, not as thesis.
meta.pov_structure: Multi-POV close third, past tense. Ben Skywalker carries the majority of chapters as primary POV. Talon Veyr carries selected chapters (Ch 8 'Waste Runoff', Ch 22 'Maro Tess'). Single-chapter POVs: Commander Elya Rane (Ch 1 hook, through her death), Sela Dray (Ch 25 'Some Places Remember Too Loudly', Ch 28 'Tavi'), Aevyn Soris (Ch 30 'Opening'), Colonel Maro Tess (opens Ch 20 PP2 Squeeze, full POV Ch 37 'A Board Cleared'). Split-POV chapters (Ben/Talon close-third alternating within the chapter): Ch 7 'Break Cover', Ch 9 'Storm Line' (FPP), Ch 14-15 archive sequence (PP1), Ch 16 'No Good Version' (Midpoint), Ch 33 'The Flood'. Ch 38 is a distant/image POV (the white-blue spark).

branch_point.divergence_point: Post-Fate of the Jedi, 47 ABY (three years after the close of FOTJ; two years after Crucible).
branch_point.divergence_description: Legacy comics did NOT happen — no Darth Krayt galactic war, no Cade Skywalker, no fall of the Galactic Alliance to the One Sith. The One Sith on Korriban still exist and remain in patient pre-emergence under Darth Krayt, glimpsed in Book 1 only as a hand and a long-game (Dorvan is a FUTURE target of an identity-shaping infiltration program, not a Book 1 puppet). Other minor adjustments allowed as the investigation requires — none yet load-bearing.

canon_constraints.continuity: Star Wars Legends (Expanded Universe), post-Fate of the Jedi, 47 ABY. Crucible (45 ABY) canonical; Legacy comics did NOT happen; the One Sith on Korriban remain in patient pre-emergence under Darth Krayt, glimpsed only as an off-page hand.
canon_constraints.divergence_point: Diverges from published Legends continuity by (a) excising the Legacy comics future entirely — no Darth Krayt galactic war, no Cade Skywalker, no fall of the Galactic Alliance to the One Sith; (b) introducing Aevyn Soris, a marginal Force-sensitive Jedi-rejected at fourteen who joined the GAG as a young adult and became Jacen Solo's side-project Force student during the Caedus period (Ben Skywalker remained Jacen's primary fourteen-year-old apprentice; Aevyn lived in the gaps); (c) introducing Jacen's unfinished holocron — a working device assembled during the LotF period systematizing Recognition and Holding — hidden on Iresh in old GAG-era survey/storage equipment near the Glasswell; (d) introducing the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation as a legitimate post-war veterans' charity whose hidden inner ring (the Vigil) preserves Jacen-derived 'clarity, resilience, steadiness, preparation' ideology and seeks to recover and finish the holocron.
canon_preserved: Ben Skywalker as Jedi Knight, son of Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade Skywalker; aged ~21 in 47 ABY.
Jacen Solo's fall to Darth Caedus during the Legacy of the Force period and his murder of Mara Jade.
Ben's service in the Galactic Alliance Guard (GAG) under Jacen as a fourteen-year-old, and Ben's later turn against Caedus by the end of the war.
The Abeloth crisis and the broader Fate of the Jedi arc (Daala, Lost Tribe of Sith, Vestara Khai), resolved before Book 1 opens.

Crucible (45 ABY): Luke, Leia, and Han have a transcendent Mortis-adjacent metaphysical encounter; Luke and Leia briefly become luminous beings before being called back; the three emerge changed and effectively retired from active galactic crisis-management work.
The Jedi Order's permanent relocation to Shedu Maad in the Hapes Cluster at the end of FOTJ (44 ABY), after the Senate voted to remove them from Coruscant following the Lost Tribe crisis.
Saba Sebatyne as Grand Master, having assumed the title at the end of FOTJ when Luke stepped down. Luke is a senior Master on the Council, still active, no longer Grand Master.
Wynn Dorvan as Chief of State of the Galactic Alliance, in return-to-normalcy mode after repeated crises (Yuuzhan Vong, Killik, Caedus, Daala, Abeloth, Lost Tribe).
Jagged Fel as Head of State of the Imperial Remnant; Tenel Ka Djo as Queen Mother of Hapes.
Vestara Khai canonically alive and active off-page under the alias 'Savara Raine' as a free-agent dark-side-trained contractor (per Crucible) — never on-page in Book 1.
Tahiri Veila as a Jedi Knight in good standing at Shedu Maad in 47 ABY, Ben's recent working colleague — single passing reference allowed, never as a Caedus reference.
The One Sith on Korriban under Darth Krayt as a real organization in patient pre-emergence, never on-page beyond a single off-page 'hand'.

Jacen Solo's Force odyssey (NJO-LotF transition) as the source-material for his later systematization of Recognition and Holding: Vergerean thought; Lumiya's Sith inheritance; experiments performed during the GAG/Caedus period.
Standard Legends Force ontology: light and dark as natural moral-polar properties; Force wounds remain wounds; holocrons as crystalline storage devices for Jedi or Sith teachings.
canon_overridden: Legacy comics continuity (Star Wars: Legacy / Cade Skywalker / Krayt-led galactic war) — entirely excised. The One Sith remain on Korriban in pre-emergence; they do not invade or seize the Galactic Alliance.

Aevyn Soris is a NEW character (not in published Legends): one of Jacen Solo's surviving Force students from the GAG/Caedus period, established as a side project running alongside Jacen's primary apprenticeship of Ben.
The duplicated wartime quarantine/survey shipment manifest personally encrypted by Jacen Solo shortly before the Battle of Shedu Maad is a NEW canonical artifact specific to this novel.

The unfinished holocron's specific contents — Jacen's systematized Recognition and Holding work as identity-shaping technique categories — are this novel's named extrapolation from Jacen's canonical Force-odyssey behavior. Compatible with established Legends; not previously named in published material.

The Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation (public charity), the Vigil (hidden inner ring), and Greyline Strategic Services (Tess's firm, which fields its own plausibly-deniable contractor teams for direct action) are NEW post-war Coruscant-political institutions introduced for this novel.

Iresh (remote wind-scoured planet near the edge of known space) and the Glasswell (taboo sinkhole/cavern beneath a mirror-lake, pale translucent mineral) are NEW Outer Rim locations introduced for this novel. Iresh's Force character — preserves charged impressions of memory/identity/decision but does NOT reveal truth or prophecy — is original to this novel and does NOT extend Mortis-adjacent mythology.
Tarn Velos Coastal Detention Works (storm-lashed industrial coastal prison world) and Civitas Archive Systems (Coruscant civic-records restoration and compliance firm) are NEW Book 1 settings.

Allana Solo / Amelia is treated as a dangerous gray zone in adversary awareness only — referenced obliquely in Ch 37 from the Vigil/One Sith POV ('the Hapan question' / 'the unresolved succession thread'). Never named on-page; never enters Ben's awareness. Her identity remains publicly deniable in-universe.
style_constraints: Capitalize 'Human' per Lucasfilm style guide.
Decapitalize 'galaxy' in all contexts unless starting a sentence.
American English spellings throughout.
Star Wars vocabulary discipline: datapads not tablets, transparisteel not glass, durasteel not steel, turbolifts not elevators, comlinks not radios, blasters not guns.
'Jedi' is both singular and plural — never 'Jedis'.
'Darth' as a Sith title is capitalized when preceding a name; generic 'the Sith' lowercase.
Hyperdrive classifications, ship specifications, and planetary names match Wookieepedia entries where existing canon applies.
Do not write theme as thesis. Put theme into behavior, pressure, cost, and consequence.
Do not imitate any specific published Star Wars author's prose. Use broad franchise feel only: cinematic clarity, adventure momentum, lived-in technology, dry humor, mythic Force awe when earned.
Maintain a commercial reader-facing surface at all times: goal, obstacle, movement, reversal, hook.
When in doubt, simplify the metaphysics and clarify the physical action.
Ben should rarely name his fear directly. Other characters' reactions should often reveal it.
Talon's jokes should either move the scene, hide fear, or puncture solemnity. Random quips are not enough.
Aevyn's sympathy should arrive after dread, not before it. Never let Aevyn articulate his wound directly; surface it in fragments — a pause, a sharpness, a way his hand stills.
Sela speaks from local survival knowledge, not Force theory.
Luke is emotionally intelligent, not conveniently fooled. Never have Luke reference 'As Grand Master' for himself — he is no longer Grand Master.
The One Sith remain a background shadow in Book 1 — glimpsed or implied only, never fully revealed.
Emotion shown. Stakes clarified. Jargon minimized. Mystery preserved. Confusion avoided.
The story should always make the current scene goal, immediate obstacle, result, and next danger legible to a Star Wars-aware reader who has not recently read the full Legends timeline.

Explain only what the reader needs for the current emotional or plot decision. Keep exposition packets short (1-3 sentences). Return immediately to action, dialogue, or character reaction. Repeat essential context in different emotional forms rather than dumping it once.

Investigation reader-facing vocabulary stays in physical thriller terms: fragment, duplicate manifest, quarantine disguise, archive, Foundation link, Iresh manifest/authorization. Avoid stacking abstract internal-system labels (no 'routing-index layer', 'black-channel routing grammar', 'stripped transfer shell', 'dead-channel ping', 'transfer node').
No paragraph contains more than one invented bureaucratic/technical term. Every technical phrase translated to immediate human stakes within two sentences.
Avoid 'system' as the default GAG metaphor; prefer logistics network, shipment trail, records chain, transfer chain, or operation.

Use 'Jacen' for the pre-fall identity (mentor / cousin / Force teacher Ben once trusted). Use 'Caedus' for the Sith-Lord identity (the war crimes, the murder of Mara). POV characters choose between them by emotional load: Ben moves between both; Aevyn refuses 'Caedus' and uses 'Jacen' only; Aelia privately thinks of him as Jacen but never publicly defends 'Darth Caedus'; Tess avoids both names in operational dialogue.

GAG = Galactic Alliance Guard. The full name appears once on first use (Ch 1 or Ch 2 narration), abbreviation thereafter. Same convention for the Foundation (Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation, then 'the Foundation').

Crucible aftermath (Luke's post-Mortis state) is implication only — one quiet line of texture in Ch 3 first holo call (tired in a way Ben doesn't remember; eyes further away; longer pauses). Ben notices and does NOT ask. Mortis is never named on-page.

Vestara Khai: mention only (Vara Senn's archive scar-tissue line in Ch 14-15). Vestara is active off-page as 'Savara Raine'; the drafter writes Ben's reaction with the active threat in mind but never makes the resonance explicit on the page.
Tahiri Veila: at most one passing reference if natural; never as a Caedus reference.

Han, Leia, Allana, Jaina: mention only or wholly off-page. Han and Leia are post-Crucible retired; Allana is treated as a dangerous gray zone in adversary awareness only (Ch 37 oblique); Jaina is deliberately excluded.
Mortis monolith / Father-Son-Daughter mythology: not used as plot. The Crucible texture is Luke's unspoken aftermath only; Iresh's Force character is its own simpler thing.

Inspector Cale Dorrin remains grounded: official access, records checks, scene limits, procedural pushback, and legal friction only; he is not a third lead, secret mentor, corrupt ally, hidden GAG survivor, or doomed mentor.

Allana / Amelia may appear only as a brief ordinary-life Shedu Maad texture beat or near-cameo under the Amelia identity; she is not plot-active, not a POV, not a source of visions, and not told about Elya message.
Ben/Talon friendship must form through behavior rather than declaration; Talon future-call offer is plain and grounded, with humor that undercuts sentiment rather than becoming abstract poetry.
Ben GAG/Jacen self-definition must show through choices, not speeches: he is not becoming Luke mirror or Jacen echo.

voice_definition.pov_approach: Multi-POV close third-person limited, past tense. Primary POV: Ben Skywalker (~28 of 38 chapters). Selected secondary POV: Talon Veyr (Ch 8 'Waste Runoff', Ch 22 'Maro Tess'). Single-chapter dedicated POVs: Commander Elya Rane (Ch 1 hook, through her death), Sela Dray (Ch 25 'Some Places Remember Too Loudly', Ch 28 'Tavi'), Aevyn Soris (Ch 30 'Opening'), Colonel Maro Tess (opens Ch 20 PP2 'Containment'; full POV Ch 37 'A Board Cleared'). Split-POV chapters with alternating in-chapter Ben/Talon close-third: Ch 7 'Break Cover', Ch 9 'Storm Line' (FPP), Ch 14-15 archive sequence (PP1), Ch 16 'No Good Version' (Midpoint), Ch 33 'The Flood'. Ch 38 'White-Blue Spark' is a distant/image POV — no character interior — the final spark below the broken Glasswell. POV labels stable per chapter per Chapter Outlines v4.1; refinement deferred to first-draft pass.
voice_definition.prose_register: Commercial post-war conspiracy thriller in space-opera register. Cinematic clarity, adventure momentum, lived-in technology, dry humor, mythic Force awe when earned. Reader pleasure before theme — the book reads first as a tense Star Wars adventure (murder, prison break, uneasy partnership, archive attack, respected charity with a hidden inner ring, offworld Force-site climax, morally dangerous ending) and only secondarily as a meditation on Jacen/Caedus, trauma, restraint, and dangerous knowledge. Sentence-level prose sits in the Allston/Zahn commercial neighborhood — clean, propulsive, short paragraphs, intelligent characters who sound intelligent without lecturing. Technical / institutional detail handled as character not lecture in the Traviss neighborhood. Aevyn's interior precision-with-buried-wound anchors to Tana French's controlled-mystery interiority as a non-SW touchstone. NO specific Star Wars author is imitated. CHARACTER-FIRST RULE (bible §0C): no line wiser, cooler, or more poetic than the character would naturally be.

reference_authors.author: Aaron Allston
reference_authors.what_to_emulate: REGISTER SAMPLE — NOT a voice template. Use as sentence-level rhythm and dialogue-density reference for Talon Veyr's voice and the Ben/Talon partnership tempo. Emulate: dialogue-forward scene construction; ensemble POV piloting; dry, integrated humor that moves the scene rather than decorates it; political/institutional worldbuilding delivered through argument rather than exposition; prison-and-procedural texture that earns its tension through small physical details (sea wall, storm shutters, camera lag, guard habits); buddy-cop friction that doesn't dilute serious stakes. Benchmark works: Wraith Squadron, Iron Fist, Mercy Kill; Betrayal (LotF book 1) for ensemble POV piloting circa this era.
reference_authors.what_to_avoid: Do NOT lean into the comic-relief register when scenes are darkening — the book's Act 3 is genuinely grim and the Talon humor valve must shut. Do NOT copy Allston's chapter-as-vignette structural rhythm; The Unfinished Shadow runs chapters as dramatic units of variable scene count, not Allston-style rotating-cast snapshots. Do NOT imitate his prose as a voice template; the bible forbids author-imitation and Talon must remain a specific character, not 'an Allston wraith'.

reference_authors.author: Timothy Zahn
reference_authors.what_to_emulate: REGISTER SAMPLE — NOT a voice template. Use as sentence-level rhythm and prose-discipline reference for Colonel Maro Tess's calm operational antagonist register and for Ben Skywalker's POV interiority discipline. Emulate: clean, precise, efficient prose; dialogue that advances plot and reveals character simultaneously; intelligent antagonists who sound intelligent without lecturing; tactical clarity in action scenes; short paragraphs; sentences that do their work and get out of the way. Benchmark works: Heir to the Empire, Specter of the Past as register anchors. Working rule from the Ruusan voice block: 'When in doubt about prose choices, ask whether this sentence would appear in a Zahn novel — if it is ornate or introspective beyond a line or two, the answer is no.'
reference_authors.what_to_avoid: Zahn's prose can run emotionally cool — functional rather than felt. Ben's POV needs warmth that Zahn-clear sentences alone do not carry; carry the warmth through behavior, body language, and the small private moments (Ben covering an old GAG sender code before he realizes; Ben taking the half-sandwich from a Civitas coworker; Ben tightening his hand around the table edge when he answers Luke 'Somewhere it can't hurt anyone'). Do NOT import Specter-era political-thriller framing — this is a conspiracy thriller, not a senate-procedural.

reference_authors.author: Karen Traviss
reference_authors.what_to_emulate: REGISTER SAMPLE — NOT a voice template. Use as sentence-level rhythm and texture reference for the GAG investigation register: institutional and procedural detail handled as CHARACTER rather than as lecture. Emulate: how a former operator narrates logistics, manifests, transfer corrections, and quarantine classifications in the same breath as fear and exhaustion; compressed expert dialogue between Iressa and Talon that communicates competence through implication; respect for non-Force-sensitive characters' moral weight (Talon, Iressa, Elya, Sela). Benchmark works: Republic Commando series (Hard Contact through Order 66); Imperial Commando: 501st; her Mandalorian texture as a model for institution-as-character.
reference_authors.what_to_avoid: Do NOT import Traviss's polemical authorial framing — the drafter must not editorialize about the Jedi Order through the narrator. The investigation IS critical of GAG and the Vigil (by design) but the critique lands through PERSONAL CONSEQUENCE (Elya's dead body, Iressa's lost respectable life, Talon's ruined record) rather than thesis. Do NOT lean on Mandalorian iconography or Mando'a vocabulary — there are no Mandalorians on-page in Book 1.

reference_authors.author: Tana French
reference_authors.what_to_emulate: NON-STAR-WARS REGISTER SAMPLE. Use exclusively as a sentence-level rhythm reference for Aevyn Soris's precision-with-buried-wound interior register and for Ben's post-PP2 emotional pressure passages. Emulate: controlled, exact interiority that lets the wound surface in fragments rather than confession; long sentences that trail into pause-marked fragments when the speaker brushes the thing they will not say; mystery-genre discipline of revealing only what the POV character can bear to know in this moment. Benchmark works: In the Woods, The Likeness, Broken Harbor.
reference_authors.what_to_avoid: Do NOT import French's contemporary urban-Ireland setting register or her police-procedural beats — Aevyn is not a detective and the Force is not a forensic system. Do NOT import French's deliberate withholding of the central explanation (e.g., the Woods conclusion) — Book 1 must resolve its central case cleanly; only the morally dangerous threads stay open. Use French ONLY for sentence-level rhythm in Aevyn's Ch 30 POV and the corridor-flashback fragment, never as a structural model.

character_voices.Ben Skywalker: REGISTER: controlled, direct, young under pressure, defensive when seen too clearly. Polite but rusty around ordinary civilian small talk — can handle danger better than a lunchroom conversation. Best emotional lines are SHORT. RHYTHM TARGET: controlled-direct. Short emotional lines (2-6 words). Mid-length action sentences. Interior reflection lands in two-to-three-sentence bursts before behavior takes over. Long introspective passages are an anti-pattern — show, then move. AVOIDANCE HABITS: says 'I'm fine' too quickly; moves into action before emotional conversation can catch him; covers old wounds with competence; gets defensive when Luke is right too gently; notices exits and threat angles without meaning to. GOOD: "I said I've got it." / "That doesn't make it better." / "I know what it looks like." / "I was fourteen." "That's not an excuse. It's a fact." / "I'm not doing that to her." / "Gone where?" "Somewhere it can't hurt anyone." "That wasn't what I asked." "I know." AVOID: "I fear that Jacen's shadow still lives within me." Never have Ben repeatedly ask himself 'Am I becoming Jacen?' — let other characters react to him before he admits what they saw. BETTER: Ben looked at the hostage, then at Vara, and hated that he knew another way. VULNERABLE TO: mentions of Mara; Jacen's old training phrases; Luke seeing through him; Talon refusing to let him simplify GAG; Aevyn knowing private Jacen-shaped details. CHARACTER DANGER: wants meaning, not darkness — his most dangerous choices are also his most defensible ones.
character_voices.Talon Veyr: REGISTER: quick, irreverent, practical, never solemn unless the valve shuts. When he does say something serious it lands because he avoids doing that. Jokes are not random — they MUST move the scene, hide fear, or puncture solemnity. RHYTHM TARGET: fast-irreverent. Comma-heavy. Sentence fragments allowed for tempo. Dialogue-forward; interior in short bursts. Long sentences arrive ONLY when the valve shuts and the joke fails. AVOIDANCE HABITS: jokes before answering honestly; deflects gratitude; makes fear sound like irritation; turns vulnerability into a complaint; calls Ben 'Skywalker' when guarded, 'Ben' when trust slips through. STOPS JOKING when: Tess, prison routines, civilian deaths tied to his old authorizations, children inside security systems, Ben being fourteen in GAG, anyone saying 'necessary' too smoothly. GOOD: "Good. I love careful. Careful is what people say before asking me to crawl through something illegal." / "That's not a lockdown. That's a kidnapping with paperwork." / "'I'm fine.' 'You're bleeding.' 'I'm expanding the definition.'" / "Any room with that many clean badges has done something expensive to deserve them." / "I was in government work. We called that plausible." / "He said logistics would teach me scale. It mostly taught me how easy it is to lose people in paperwork." AVOID: "My trauma has left me distrustful of institutions." BETTER: "No one builds that many exits unless they plan to leave someone else behind." CRAFT NOTE: let the jokes occasionally fail — when Talon stays silent the pressure underneath should land.
character_voices.Iressa Vossk: REGISTER: brisk, transactional, office-cynical. Uses invoices, fees, corporate language, and professional irritation as armor. Sounds like someone with a calendar invite and a hidden blaster she will deny owning. RHYTHM TARGET: clipped-bureaucratic. Sentence-level efficiency. Short declaratives interspersed with professional irritation. Long sentences only when reconstructing manifests — and even those compress technical detail into character beat. AVOIDANCE HABITS: denies knowing people she clearly knows; charges fees when frightened; uses professional language to describe criminal skills; pretends not to care while preserving names and evidence; keeps exits she insists do not exist. GOOD: "I have a calendar invite in twelve minutes and a fake name with dental benefits. Start by apologizing." / "'I do compliance.' 'You forge records.' 'That is an ugly word for user-corrected metadata.'" / "This was not a clerical duplicate. Someone cloned a shipment identity and dressed a secret up as medical cargo." / "Jedi complication fee." / "'Talon owes me money.' 'How much?' 'That depends on how irritating he is in the next five minutes.'" AVOID: "I built a fragile life to hide from my past." BETTER: "Do you know how hard it is to get a respectable job after a war crime adjacency problem?" DEATH RULE: she dies actively denying the enemy a clean copy and transmitting the dying package. NOT a martyrdom lesson for Ben. Her final beat is herself — practical irritation, file anger, or one last debt/fee joke rather than sentimental sacrifice.
character_voices.Aelia Vandros: REGISTER: warm, precise, composed, socially powerful. Rarely raises her voice — her danger is credibility, not volume. Never publicly defends 'Darth Caedus'; civic / memorial / therapeutic language only (clarity, resilience, steadiness, continuity, preparation). Privately thinks of Jacen as Jacen. RHYTHM TARGET: warm-civic-controlled. Longer sentences than the other antagonists. Subordinate clauses for graciousness. Never two emphatic words in a row. Polished cadence that beats Ben socially before he understands he is losing. AVOIDANCE HABITS: translates moral horror into civic language; corrects simplifications gently; uses grief as both truth and shield; remembers names; writes condolence notes by hand; uses courtesy as control. GOOD: "I write to the families every year, Master Skywalker. Not because it heals them. It does not. But because someone should remember the names without needing a trial transcript." / "You are very young. That is not an insult. It is only a fact people forget when reading your family name." / "I am not asking you to forgive him. I am asking whether the dead are better served by pretending no one learned anything at all." / "The crimes were real. So were the failures that came before them." AVOID: "Jacen's crimes contained necessary truths." BETTER: "Some people hesitate until the casualty lists become easier to print than the orders." CRAFT NOTE: Aelia must beat Ben SOCIALLY before she is exposed operationally. If she becomes obviously evil too early she loses power. Warmth must remain real through the end.
character_voices.Bren Korda: REGISTER: clean, controlled, administrative menace. Smooth with superiors, polite in public, cruel through process, never openly messy when witnesses matter. More frightening when he makes cruelty sound appropriate; never a thug. RHYTHM TARGET: procedural-clean. Declarative sentences in complete-paragraph units. Bureaucratic rhythm: the form of concern with the function of refusal. AVOIDANCE HABITS: hides threats inside procedure; uses proper channels as weapons; makes others seem unreasonable for noticing danger; treats compassion as a security vulnerability. GOOD: "You are welcome to file a complaint. I can recommend the appropriate office." / "This is a memorial facility, Master Skywalker. I would ask you to remember where you are." / "Security is mostly preventing emotional people from making permanent decisions." / "Veyr. I assumed they had better locks." AVOID: "I am corrupt but respectable." BETTER: "Procedure exists to protect everyone. Even people who find it inconvenient." CRAFT NOTE: Talon's humor THINS or stops in any room Korda enters — Korda makes Talon feel seen in the worst way.
character_voices.Colonel Maro Tess: REGISTER: plain, calm, operational. NO villain poetry. Does not posture. Does not explain more than required. Uses Talon's first name when it asserts ownership — Talon hates it. RHYTHM TARGET: plain-operational. Declarative. No subordinate clauses for ornament. Each sentence carries one fact or one instruction. Maximum economy. Two-word lines are allowed and preferred when they land. AVOIDANCE HABITS: turns people into categories (exposed, recoverable, lost); treats failures as logistics; removes sentiment from decisions; uses first names when asserting ownership. GOOD: "'Korda can carry the public version.' 'He's dead.' 'That helps.'" / "'Iresh failed.' 'Completely?' 'No.'" / "Skywalker moved as trained." / "Do not punish panic. Use it or remove it." / "Talon always did understand exits." / "You saved the people in front of you. You lost the people I needed you to think about." AVOID: "History belongs to those who manage its losses." BETTER: "The report needs one responsible name. Korda's will do." CRAFT NOTE: Tess is terrifying because he is NORMAL. Failure does not embarrass him; it gives him new categories.
character_voices.Aevyn Soris: REGISTER: quiet, exact, wounded underneath. Speaks SOFTER when angry, not louder. Dislikes generic praise. Replays exact wording of old dismissals. Aligns tools at exact angles. Refuses 'Caedus' — uses 'Jacen' only. RHYTHM TARGET: quiet-precise. Sentences trimmed to load-bearing words. Periods over commas. Long sentences land ONLY when the wound flashes through — then trail off into pause-marked fragment. Tana French interiority register; the corridor flashback surfaces as image, never speech. AVOIDANCE HABITS: aligns tools at exact angles; corrects language when others are imprecise; controls his tone carefully; refuses broad emotional confession; treats his unstable lightsaber like an argument he keeps trying to perfect; replays the exact wording of old dismissals when alone. WHAT MAKES HIM CRACK: being called weak or insufficient; generic praise (he knows how to recognize the polite no underneath); Jacen reduced to only Caedus; Ben having Jedi training, family, Jacen's primary attention, and survival; Ben using Jacen's lessons while denying Aevyn the holocron; any reference to 'placement' or 'measuring'. GOOD: "They said I had patience. They meant no." / "Do not call him that." / "He taught you to count exits before faces, didn't he?" / "You buried the lesson. You still used it." / "The Jedi measure what they can use. Jacen measured what could grow." AVOID: "The Jedi rejected me and Jacen validated my existence." AVOID: "Jacen had Tahiri. Jacen had Ben. I had what was left." (THE WOUND STAYS UNSPOKEN.) BETTER: "They told me to keep practicing. They said it kindly." CRAFT NOTE: frightening FIRST; sympathy arrives later in cracks, never speeches. The corridor flashback (Jacen leaving a Recognition session with Aevyn to walk off with fourteen-year-old Ben) surfaces as image-fragment in Aevyn's Ch 30 POV — NEVER as exposition. NEVER as speech.
character_voices.Sela Dray: REGISTER: practical, blunt, grounded. Never mystical unless quoting local phrasing, and even then she undercuts it. Authority comes from lived local knowledge, not Force theory. RHYTHM TARGET: blunt-local. Short. Concrete nouns. Rules expressed as conditionals: 'If X, then Y.' Refuses metaphor. The blunt speaker who is funny because she refuses awe. AVOIDANCE HABITS: turns worry into irritation; refuses mystical language; gives rules instead of explanations; treats Jedi questions as offworlder overcomplication. GOOD: "If the chimes stop, run. You can argue about what it means after you are not dead." / "That is the route offworlders built. It is not the same thing as the way out." / "You people always ask what it means. It means don't go down there." / "You saved him. That does not make this place yours." / "Tavi knew better. That is what makes me angry." AVOID: "The Glasswell is a sacred place of memory." BETTER: "Some places remember too loudly. Locals call that a warning. Offworlders call it research." NAMING ARC: calls Ben 'Skywalker' through Ch 28; shifts to 'Ben' from Ch 34 onward — conditional trust only, never granted ownership of her home.
character_voices.Luke Skywalker: REGISTER: simple, warm, precise. Wise but NOT poetic. NOT a fortune cookie. Slower than he used to be (post-Crucible — implication only, never named). RHYTHM TARGET: simple-warm-quieter-than-he-used-to-be. Short. Paternal. Pauses indicated by paragraph breaks. ONE image of distance per holo scene (eyes further away, longer pauses, tired in a way Ben doesn't quite remember). AVOIDANCE HABITS: gives room when he wants to hold on; uses questions instead of accusations; lets silence work longer than Ben wants; defers institutional decisions to Saba even when Ben wants him to override them. GOOD: "You answered quickly. That usually means you decided before I asked." / "'You want this to be yours.' 'Someone sent it to me.' 'That is not what I meant.'" / "I trust you. I'm also worried. Those are not opposites." / "This needs to go to Saba. She'll do it right. I know that's not what you want to hear." / "'Gone where?' 'Somewhere it can't hurt anyone.' 'That wasn't what I asked.'" AVOID: "I sense you are walking a dangerous path." / "As Grand Master, I must…" (HE IS NO LONGER GRAND MASTER — never have Luke reference the title for himself.) BETTER: "Ben, look at me. Are you choosing this, or chasing it?" POST-CRUCIBLE TEXTURE: tired eyes; longer pauses; eyes seeming further away even when looking directly at Ben. ONE quiet line of this per holo scene. Mortis NEVER named. Ben notices and does NOT ask.
character_voices.Vara Senn: REGISTER: cutting, confident, impatient. Less refined than Aevyn, more theatrical than Tess. Enjoys needling. Uses old Sith / Lost Tribe superiority as armor. RHYTHM TARGET: aggressive-theatrical. Short jabs interspersed with status-asserting flourishes. Adjectives carrying contempt. Tone faster than Tess, blunter than Aelia. AVOIDANCE HABITS: dominates before she can be dismissed; turns insecurity into contempt; escalates when she feels ordinary. GOOD: "'They told stories about you on Kesh.' 'I doubt they were accurate.' 'No. They made you sound taller.'" / "'Vestara Khai.' Ben's guard did not move. 'But not nothing.'" / "Jedi restraint. Very pretty. Very slow." / "I do not need to beat you, Skywalker. I only need you looking at me." AVOID: "I represent the crude dark-side temptation before Aevyn's refined mirror." BETTER: "You guard the door. I'll take what she knows." CRAFT NOTE: tests Ben physically and emotionally; loses combat pressure quickly and shifts to hostage/memory pressure. NOT the main Force antagonist. Disappears into the contractor pool after PP1 — not on-page after Ch 15.
character_voices.Commander Elya Rane: REGISTER: practical, tense, grounded. Thinks in files and fields to avoid thinking in bodies. Uses procedural caution to manage fear. Tells herself she is only verifying until she knows she is already choosing. RHYTHM TARGET: tired-procedural. Mid-length sentences with institutional vocabulary held at arm's length. The voice of someone who has spent years naming horrors as records-management issues. AVOIDANCE HABITS: thinks in files and fields to avoid thinking in bodies; uses procedural caution to manage fear; tells herself she is only verifying. GOOD (narration register): "Emergency custody became protected transfer. Interrogation became review. Children became approval fields if no one moved their names in time." / "She had not saved Ben Skywalker. Not really. She had only made history work harder to blame a child." / "We need to talk. I found something dangerous. It started in GAG. Come alone." AVOID: "The moral legacy of the Galactic Alliance Guard continues to haunt the postwar political order." BETTER: "Elya had learned that governments did not bury crimes all at once. They renamed them first." CRAFT NOTE: briefly human before she dies — practical fear, one regret, one sign of competence, the memory of Ben's wrong approval field. The opening must NOT stall on her; she carries Ch 1 and then the plot moves.
character_voices.Elya Rane:
Practical, tense, grounded. She should orient new readers to GAG through consequences, not lectures.

Good Elya register: Emergency custody became protected transfer. Interrogation became review. Children became approval fields if no one moved their names in time. She had not saved Ben Skywalker. Not really. She had only made history work harder to blame a child. “GAG is still active. One of Jacen’s last orders has two lives. Come alone. — E.R.” Avoid Elya register: “The moral legacy of the Galactic Alliance Guard continues to haunt the postwar political order.” Better: Elya had learned that governments did not bury crimes all at once. They renamed them first.

Minimal in the opening. Dry, practical, tired.

Careful, records-trained, watches systems more than people until people become dangerous.

Do not overextend Elya. She needs to be human enough to matter, not so detailed that the opening stalls.
character_voices.Cale Dorrin:
Plain, procedural, dry. No grand speeches. No secret-mentor warmth. He speaks in case terms and lets discomfort show as irritation.

“You can sense whatever you like. I need something I can put in front of a magistrate.” “I checked Rane’s old assignment logs. Veyr’s name came up. That does not make him innocent. It makes him relevant.” “You asked me for lawful access. I gave it to you. Twelve hours later the prison is burning and my witness is gone.” “I can open a door for you, Master Skywalker. I cannot keep it open after you blow the wall out.”

Dry, tired, practical. He is funny because he is not impressed by mythic urgency.

Professional, skeptical, controlled. Will help when evidence gives him a reason. Will push back when Ben acts like a Jedi instinct can replace a record.

Do not make Dorrin too important. He is not the third lead, not corrupt, not secretly Vigil, and not another doomed mentor. His value is practical access and grounded pushback.

anti_slop_rules.description: Two-tier anti-slop rules for The Unfinished Shadow. The twelve derived_rules are book-level prose discipline lifted from Planning Bible §0A / §0C / §0D and the locked detour resolutions. The line_level_rules merge config/negative_constraints.yaml AI-tells with book-specific phrase prohibitions. The voice checker enforces both tiers.

derived_rules.name: Character-first prose (bible §0C)
derived_rules.content: No line should sound wiser, cooler, or more poetic than the character would naturally be. Use humor, irritation, silence, avoidance, practical choices, and physical behavior to show emotion. Keep metaphor light and POV-specific. When a line sounds 'cool,' check whether it sounds like the character.

derived_rules.name: Theme through behavior (bible §0A)
derived_rules.content: Do NOT write theme as thesis. Put theme into behavior, pressure, cost, and consequence. Theme should be obvious in hindsight, not announced in prose.

derived_rules.name: Investigation vocabulary (bible §0D)
derived_rules.content: Investigation reader-facing vocabulary stays in physical thriller terms: fragment, duplicate manifest, quarantine disguise, archive, Foundation link, Iresh manifest/authorization. NO stacking abstract internal-system labels. NO more than one invented bureaucratic/technical term per paragraph in Act 2. Every technical phrase translates to immediate human stakes within two sentences. Avoid 'system' as the default GAG metaphor; prefer logistics network, shipment trail, records chain, transfer chain, operation.

derived_rules.name: Reader orientation (bible §0B)
derived_rules.content: Emotion shown. Stakes clarified. Jargon minimized. Mystery preserved. Confusion avoided. The reader should always understand the current scene goal, immediate obstacle, result, and next danger. Exposition packets: 1-3 sentences. Return immediately to action, dialogue, or character reaction. Repeat essential context in different emotional forms rather than dumping it once.

derived_rules.name: Show-before-name (Force, theme, wound)
derived_rules.content: Render body-experience first; name the mechanism second. Diagnostic vocabulary (Recognition and Holding, Jacen-derived crisis logic) is earned by experiential rendering and may not arrive on the page until the body has felt the thing. The reader feels the wrongness before the word for the wrongness arrives.

derived_rules.name: Jacen vs Caedus naming discipline
derived_rules.content: Use 'Jacen' for the pre-fall identity (cousin, mentor). Use 'Caedus' for the Sith-Lord identity. POVs choose by emotional load: Ben slides between both; Aevyn refuses 'Caedus' and uses 'Jacen' only; Aelia privately thinks 'Jacen' but never publicly defends 'Darth Caedus'; Tess avoids both names operationally; Talon uses 'Caedus' when contemptuous, 'Jacen' when Ben is in earshot and he is trying not to wound him.

derived_rules.name: Crucible / Mortis implication-only rule
derived_rules.content: Crucible aftermath is Luke's UNSPOKEN texture. ONE quiet line per holo scene (tired eyes, longer pauses, eyes further away even when looking directly at Ben). Ben notices and does NOT ask. Mortis is NEVER named on-page. Never have a character explain what happened to Luke at Crucible. A reader who knows Crucible reads it as Mortis aftermath; a reader who does not reads it as a father aging into something new.

derived_rules.name: Allana / Amelia gray-zone rule
derived_rules.content: Allana / Amelia is NEVER named on-page and NEVER enters Ben's awareness. The only acknowledgment is the Ch 37 oblique Tess-POV reference to 'the Hapan question' / 'the unresolved succession thread' — Vigil/adversary awareness only. Her identity remains publicly deniable in-universe.

derived_rules.name: Iressa death rule
derived_rules.content: Iressa dies actively denying the enemy a clean copy and transmitting the two-part dying package (documentary chain + identity-shaping revelation). Her final beat is HERSELF — practical irritation, file anger, or one last debt/fee joke rather than sentimental martyrdom. Ben carries guilt; Iressa keeps agency.

derived_rules.name: Climax: rescue first, duel second
derived_rules.content: The Ch 31-32 Glasswell climax saves Tavi, Sela's locals, and others BEFORE the Ben/Aevyn lightsaber duel begins. Ben's dangerous Jacen-shaped choice emerges from saving lives, not from aggression. The rescue should clearly be heroic before it becomes unsettling.

derived_rules.name: Coda holocron omission
derived_rules.content: Ben's morally incomplete ending BEGINS in Act 3 (Ch 33-34), not just in the coda. The Ch 36 'Gone where?' exchange with Luke is technically true and morally incomplete — Luke senses the incompleteness and does NOT force the answer. The drafter MUST keep Ben's voice steady while the body says what the words don't (hand tightening on the edge of a table, breath caught, eyes that don't quite meet Luke's).

derived_rules.name: Sentence-level rhythm targets per POV
derived_rules.content: Ben: controlled-direct, short emotional lines, mid-length action. Talon: fast-irreverent, comma-heavy, fragments for tempo, dialogue-forward. Aevyn: quiet-precise, trimmed to load-bearing words, periods over commas, long sentences ONLY when the wound flashes through. Tess: plain-operational, declarative, one fact or instruction per sentence, two-word lines preferred when they land. Aelia: warm-civic-controlled, subordinate clauses for graciousness, never two emphatic words in a row. Sela: blunt-local, short, concrete nouns, rules as conditionals. Luke: simple-warm-quieter-than-he-used-to-be, paternal, pauses indicated by paragraph breaks, one image of distance per holo scene.

derived_rules.name: Dorrin grounded official-contact rule
derived_rules.content: Dorrin brings lawful access, records checks, scene limits, legal friction, and procedural pushback. Do not make him a secret mentor, third lead, doomed ally, hidden survivor, or corrupt reveal.

derived_rules.name: Ben/Talon future-call rule
derived_rules.content: The Ben/Talon friendship resolves through behavior and accountability. The future-call offer is plain: if Ben needs him, call; Talon complains first, then comes. Keep humor grounded in practical Star Wars annoyances.

derived_rules.name: Ben self-definition engine
derived_rules.content: Ben is not becoming Luke mirror or Jacen echo. Show him learning how to use what he survived without letting it own him through choices, not thesis dialogue.

derived_rules.name: Allana / Amelia ordinary-life cameo rule
derived_rules.content: A brief Shedu Maad cameo or near-cameo under Amelia identity is allowed as ordinary family texture only. She is not plot-active, not told about Elya message, not a POV, and not a source of visions.

Never use 'Breath he didn't know he was holding'
Never use 'Could not help but notice'
Never use 'The kind of pain that'
Never use 'The kind of silence that'
Never use 'The kind of weight that'
Never use 'Like a skip in a recording'
Never use 'The body keeps the score'
Never have Ben Skywalker articulate 'Am I becoming Jacen?' in interior monologue — show the buried fear through behavior; let other characters react before he admits what they saw.
Never have Aevyn Soris speak the corridor-flashback wound out loud — it surfaces as image-fragment only.
Never have Aevyn say 'The Jedi rejected me and Jacen validated my existence' or any variant that articulates the side-project framing directly.
Never have Luke Skywalker reference 'As Grand Master' for himself — he is no longer Grand Master; Saba Sebatyne holds the title.
Never name 'Mortis' on-page. Never have a character explain what happened to Luke at Crucible.
Never name Allana / Amelia on-page. Never have her enter Ben's awareness.
Never have Aelia Vandros publicly defend 'Darth Caedus' or use overtly Sith-coded language — her register is civic, memorial, therapeutic.
Never have Colonel Maro Tess speak in villain poetry, theatrical menace, or moral monologue — calm operational dialogue only, treats people as logistics.
Never have Sela Dray explain the Glasswell in mystical or Force-theoretical terms — local survival rules only.
Never have Talon Veyr make a quip that doesn't move the scene, hide fear, or puncture solemnity — random quips dilute the pressure valve.
Never frame Iressa Vossk's death as a martyrdom lesson for Ben — she dies with agency, on her own terms, denying the enemy a clean copy.
Never use 'the ambient hum of the Force' or any variant that renders the Force as a measurable background phenomenon — Legends Force is experiential, not technical.
Never use 'energy field' as a description of the Force in narration.
Never use 'midi-chlorians' — Disney Canon concept; not in Legends-EU.
Never use a Mando'a vocabulary item (the book has no Mandalorians on-page in Book 1).

Never use 'kyber bleeding' or any Disney-canon variant for Aevyn's white-blue blade — its color is the natural result of a salvaged outside-tradition crystal plus a self-built focusing rig, not Sith corruption ritual.
Never use 'the dark side called to him' as a tell that Ben is being tempted — the Jacen-shaped choice arrives dressed as compassion, urgency, and competence, not as seduction.
Never use 'galaxy' capitalized in narration unless it begins a sentence.
Never use 'Jedis' as a plural — 'Jedi' is both singular and plural.
Never use 'galactic' as a generic intensifier ('galactically important', 'galactic-scale') — it is a directional adjective in Star Wars vocabulary, not a substitute for 'very'.
Never use 21st-century pop-culture references, real-world brand names, or internet idioms.
Never use 'tablet', 'laptop', 'cell phone', 'radio', 'sonar', 'LIDAR' — see canon.json anachronistic_terms for the full mapping.

Never use 'the kind of silence that', 'the kind of weight that', 'the kind of pain that' — banned-phrase pattern from the global constraints; restated here because the prose is prone to it in mood beats.

Every chapter ending with a reflective sigh or 'little did they know' hook.
Characters nodding, smiling, or raising eyebrows as default body language.

voice_definition.force_description_guidelines:
The Force is rendered through experiential and mystical language — NOT clinical or scientific framing. Avoid 'energy field' as description; avoid 'ambient hum of the Force' entirely. Luke's generation understands the Force as a LIVING PRESENCE, not a measurable phenomenon.

BODY BEFORE NAME: Force perception lands as body-sensation first; narration or characters name what they sensed only after the body has felt it. Reaching for the Force returns texture, density, direction — never an explanation. Recognition and Holding may be NAMED in dialogue (Iressa transmits them in Ch 15-16; Ben reads them off the cache in Ch 29) but never explained beyond their plain-language consequences. Plain-language consequence of the Midpoint revelation: 'It's Jacen's notebook on how to shape people from the inside, and the Vigil wants to finish the work.'

IRESH MEMORY MECHANIC: Iresh PRESERVES charged impressions of memory, identity, and decision under pressure. Impressions felt strongly on Iresh are emotionally charged but NOT objectively reliable. Sela's practical translation: 'Do not trust what you feel here just because it feels strong.' Iresh does NOT show the future, reveal truth, or grant prophecy.

THE GLASSWELL: a natural site Jacen Solo exploited for practical concealment — NOT a Sith temple, Jedi ruin, or mystical treasure chamber. Cache hidden in old offworld survey / GAG-era storage equipment. Forcing the Glasswell to remember the moment Jacen sealed it (Aevyn's Ch 30 act) destabilizes the natural site: water enters, mineral supports crack, scaffolds break. The mythic and the physical converge through STRUCTURAL FAILURE, not mystical reveal.

AEVYN'S BLADE: the cold white-blue unstable lightsaber is a VISUAL TELL, NOT exposition. Its instability escalates when Ben successfully uses Jacen-derived crisis logic during the Ch 31-32 duel. Aevyn registers Ben as Jacen's primary student through the blade's behavior before either of them speaks the fact. The drafter MUST let the image do the work; explain nothing.

BEN'S JACEN-DERIVED CRISIS LOGIC: not a Force technique — a mindset. How to see panic, timing, exits, the whole room, and the cost of hesitation. Surfaces SUBTLY in Ben's behavior throughout Acts 1-2 (Ch 6 visitor room, Ch 7 prison breakout). Surfaces DECISIVELY at the Glasswell rescue (Ch 31). Ben experiences it as discomfort with his own competence; other characters see it before he names it. Aevyn's recognition of it is the duel's pivot.
voice_definition.pacing_feel:
Conspiracy-thriller cadence across Acts 1-2 (murder, fragment, prison break, archive attack, charity reveal). Operational-thriller acceleration through the PP2 Squeeze (Ch 20). Strange-world expedition register across Act 3 (Iresh wind, paths, chimes, Tavi rescue, Glasswell collapse). Rescue-then-duel climax (Ch 31-32 as one sustained beat). Quiet coda with morally incomplete preservation (Ch 35-38).

WORD-COUNT TARGET: 105,000 words across 38 chapters (~2,760 words per chapter average) with deliberate variance. RUN LONGER than average: Ch 1 (consolidated Elya hook); Ch 11 (Skywalker apartment introduction); Ch 16 (Midpoint Iressa transmission + Luke + Saba calls + Ben's pivot); Ch 20 (PP2 three-part Squeeze + apartment return + Luke holo); Ch 31-32 (Glasswell rescue + duel as sustained climax beat). RUN SHORTER than average: the connective-tissue chapters (Ch 3, Ch 5, Ch 10, Ch 21, Ch 23, Ch 26, Ch 27, Ch 35, Ch 37, Ch 38).

BEAT-ON-BEAT SCENE RHYTHM: every chapter must have IMMEDIATE STORY ACTION even if the reader misses the theme. Goal / obstacle / movement / reversal / hook. The chapter ends with a question the reader carries to the next chapter. End hooks per Chapter Outlines v4.1 are LOCKED — do not soften or move them.

SCENE-COUNT DISCIPLINE: most chapters carry ONE load-bearing scene. Multi-scene chapters (Ch 7, Ch 8 split-POV, Ch 14-15 archive, Ch 16 Midpoint, Ch 20 PP2, Ch 31-32 climax) earn the split because each scene carries a distinct turning point, mission, and emotional arc. Do NOT pad single-scene chapters with redundant beats.
voice_definition.narrative_voice_notes:
READER PROMISE: A post-Fate of the Jedi Legends conspiracy thriller written to commercial-novel quality. Murder, clue, prison break, uneasy partnership, archive attack, respected charity with a hidden inner ring, offworld Force-site climax, rescue, duel, and a morally dangerous ending. The reader should finish remembering a tense Star Wars adventure with Ben Skywalker, a great rogue partner, a creepy Jacen legacy mystery, an offworld Force-site climax, and a morally dangerous ending. Only AFTERWARD should the deeper themes — restraint can cost lives, Jacen's crisis logic can save lives, forbidden knowledge may be necessary to heal or protect — fully settle in.

CENTRAL THEMATIC ARGUMENT: Ben's danger is not that he wants to become Jacen; it is that he wants to make sure Jacen was not meaningless. His most defensible choices and his most dangerous choices can be the same choices.

REFERENCE-AUTHOR FRAMING: The Allston / Zahn / Traviss / Tana French anchors are REGISTER SAMPLES for sentence-level rhythm and dialogue density — NOT voice templates. The bible explicitly forbids imitating any specific Star Wars author. When in doubt, the character-first prose rule (bible §0C) overrides any reference-author convention.

RESOLVED RULES FROM IDEA-SESSION: (a) Post-Crucible Luke texture is implication only — one quiet line per holo scene (tired eyes, longer pauses, eyes further away even when looking directly at Ben); Ben notices and does NOT ask; Mortis is NEVER named on-page. (b) Allana / Amelia is NEVER named on-page and NEVER enters Ben's awareness — the only acknowledgment is the Ch 37 oblique Tess-POV reference to 'the Hapan question' / 'the unresolved succession thread' in the adversary's awareness. (c) Vara Senn disappears into the contractor pool after PP1 and does NOT return on-page. (d) Aelia steps down quietly in Ch 35 with no criminal liability; private moral collapse visible, unpunished. (e) The One Sith hand in Ch 37 remains UNNAMED — off-page voice / message / presence only.

STAR WARS VOCABULARY DISCIPLINE: see canon.json canon_profile.anachronistic_terms and franchise_terminology_notes for the full mapping. The drafter MUST consult canon.json before introducing any new technology, ship class, species, or institution.

promise_payoff_ledger.promise: Why did one of Jacen's last shipments have two lives? — the central mystery.
The forced Ben/Talon partnership will outlast the case as a real partnership — not a transaction.
Restraint can cost lives — Ben will learn this not as a philosophical position but as a body lying still after he held the line.
Every door except Iresh will be closed — the institutional path, the documentary path, the legal path, the time path. Ben will go off-grid because there is no other door.
Ben will use Jacen's lessons — the crisis logic the GAG year built into him will save lives that the ordinary Jedi path cannot save.

Aelia Vandros will be socially formidable AND publicly diminished — the Foundation's real charity will be the reason Ben cannot morally flatten her, AND the reason her stepping down preserves the harm.
Sela will save Tavi and the locals through specific Iresh knowledge Ben does not have — the climax rescue will be a shared act of different competencies.
Talon will name his Glasshook/Tess wound out loud — the prison habits and the comedy valve are the cover for a confession that has to land in Ben's hearing in his own register.
Ben will preserve the unfinished holocron under a technically-true omission — his most defensible and most dangerous choice will be the same choice.
Aevyn will survive the Glasswell — the precision method that opens the book will outlast the operation that deployed it.
The One Sith long game will continue — Iresh was one chess move; Dorvan and the broader infiltration program survive Book 1's case being closed.
Luke will sense the omission and not force the answer — the father who knows is the strongest indictment the book can offer.

subplots.name: Talon / Tess Mentor Wound (Glasshook → PP2 frame)
subplots.function: Character-driven antagonist thread; the ownership wound between Talon Veyr and his former GAG mentor Colonel Maro Tess
subplots.arc_summary: Talon's prison habits (Ch 6) carry the wound silently. The FPP rescue (Ch 9) puts him back in motion. The apartment beat (Ch 11) cracks the performance. PP2 Squeeze (Ch 20) puts Tess's tradecraft fingerprint on Talon's frame — the mentor reaching across years to mark him again. Talon names Glasshook and the corridor moment 'Move her first' to Ben in Ch 22 — the wound out loud for the first time. Talon disrupts Greyline extraction at the Glasswell (Ch 33), speaking back to Tess's lesson through field work. Tess survives in Ch 37; the wound persists into Book 2.

subplots.name: Iressa's Rebuilt Respectable Life (Civitas → secondary cache)
subplots.function: Short-arc character subplot carrying the Midpoint structural pivot
subplots.arc_summary: Iressa is introduced at Civitas under her clean professional name (Ch 12); the lunchroom beat humanizes her workplace. Her secondary cache is established as a passing detail (Ch 13) — the off-record space where she does the serious reconstruction. Old GAG instincts wake at the archive (Ch 13-14). She dies preserving the dying package (Ch 15), her short arc resolving: old Iressa buried discrepancies; new Iressa preserved one. The cache is professionally raided and burned at PP2 (Ch 20) — the documentary case she died protecting is overtaken anyway. Her work outlives the body by minutes; the Midpoint pivot (Ch 16) is what her death made possible.

subplots.name: Sela & Tavi / Iresh Local Damage
subplots.function: Act 3 grounding subplot — keeps Iresh a place before it is a metaphor
subplots.arc_summary: Iresh has been damaged by offworlders before. Sela's stake is Tavi, pressured/paid by the Foundation into the Glasswell exclusion zone. Sela refuses to help at first (Ch 24); her conditional alliance comes through specific local knowledge shared without granting offworlder ownership of her home. She demonstrates Iresh's memory-preservation rules through survival vocabulary (Ch 25), not Force theory. Tavi is humanized through evidence — guide tokens, recordings, warning marks — before he becomes a rescue objective (Ch 28). Sela saves Tavi and locals at the Glasswell through knowledge Ben does not have (Ch 31, 33). Imperfect Sela/Tavi reunion (Ch 34): anger, relief, practical care, no easy sentimentality. 'You saved him. That does not make this place yours.'

subplots.name: Aelia's Grief-and-Corruption Entanglement
subplots.function: Public-face antagonist subplot — the Foundation's real charity entangled with the Vigil's hidden ideology
subplots.arc_summary: Aelia beats Ben socially at the Foundation (Ch 17) because her warmth and the charity's public work are real. Korda's presence (Ch 17-18) reveals the operational machinery beneath. Talon's manifest-correction bait surfaces Korda (Ch 18); the chase exposes an active operation (Ch 19). Tess kills Korda at PP2 (Ch 20) — Aelia sees that her cause is being managed by men who treat people as logistics. The news coverage (Ch 21) calcifies a story incompatible with Ben's evidence. Iresh fails (Ch 33). Aelia steps down quietly with no criminal liability (Ch 35) — she accepts the bleaker truth without publicly recanting. The harm persists; the Foundation survives diminished.

subplots.name: Foundation / Vigil Operational Machinery (Greyline / Greyline / Korda)
subplots.arc_summary: Aevyn's Ch 1 method (precision rather than savagery) signals the operational level. Greyline's prison snatch (Ch 7) and archive cleanup (Ch 14-15) establish the contractor arm. Korda's spotting at the Foundation (Ch 17) names the old-GAG-in-respectable-clothing layer. Talon's bait + Korda chase (Ch 18-19) yields the Iresh operational evidence. Tess's PP2 board-clearing (Ch 20) — Korda dead, Iressa's cache burned, Talon framed — is the machinery at peak operational tempo. The Iresh field camp (Ch 26) is the apparatus deployed. Aevyn forces the cache (Ch 30); the duel (Ch 32) and flood (Ch 33) collapse the operation. Foundation survives diminished in Ch 35; the machinery outlives this operation in Ch 37.

subplots.name: One Sith Long Game (off-page hand; Aevyn survival)
subplots.function: Series-spanning subplot — glimpsed in Book 1, drives Book 2+ setup
subplots.arc_summary: The One Sith on Korriban remain in patient pre-emergence under Darth Krayt. Tess's PP2 logistics (Ch 20) carry the hand's interest. The Ch 37 hand-POV coda registers Iresh as a failed but recoverable operation in a broader infiltration program. The oblique 'Hapan question' reference (Ch 37) plants Allana as future-target asset without naming her. The Ch 38 cold white-blue spark confirms Aevyn survived: stripped of the holocron, the Vigil, Tess's protection, and the identity of Jacen's unfinished student — broken-open but not destroyed. The cycle continues into Book 2.

hooks.description: Why did Jacen Solo personally encrypt a duplicated wartime shipment manifest days before Shedu Maad, and why did the hidden copy go somewhere the public shipment never went? Reader-facing form: why did one of Jacen's last shipments have two lives? Resolved at the Midpoint when Iressa's dying transmission reveals the holocron's identity-shaping purpose.
Who killed Elya Rane, and what is the precision of the method? The Force-trauma Ben senses in Ch 4 names the killer through behavior. Aevyn is unsettled into semi-revelation in Ch 27.

Is Talon Veyr the right partner, or has Ben made a catastrophic mistake breaking cover for him? The storm-line escape answers through action: Ben saves Talon physically, Talon gets them out operationally.

Whom is the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation actually protecting? Korda's spotting in Ch 17, manifest-correction bait in Ch 18, and Korda chase in Ch 19 resolve the operational connection: the Foundation is guarding an active Iresh operation.

Why is the Vigil moving on Iresh NOW? The SPP at the cache site confirms: because Aevyn can finish the holocron, because Ben's involvement accelerates the timeline, and because the cache has always been on Iresh waiting for the right student.

Can Ben use Jacen's lessons without becoming Caedus? PP1 Iressa death plants the question (restraint cost a life); Ch 31 Glasswell rescue tests it (the lessons save lives); Ch 32 duel resolves it (Ben wins by using what Jacen taught him WITHOUT surrendering ownership).

Who told Greyline where Iressa's secondary cache was? The breach point at PP2 is deliberately not identified. A coworker leaned on? A forgotten contact? A small breach Iressa herself never noticed? The unanswered version is creepier and serves the novel's institutional-decay theme. Available as a Book 2 thread or as ambient unanswered weight.

What does Ben do with the preserved unfinished holocron? Luke senses the omission in Ch 36 and does not force the answer. Talon suspects in Ch 34 and names it in Ch 34. The answer belongs to Book 2 — the cycle of Ben's morally compromised choices continuing.

Did Aevyn really survive, and what does he become after the broken certainty? Ch 38's cold white-blue spark confirms survival to the reader only — Ben, Talon, and the Order presume him dead. Book 2 seed: possible Bane-like emergence from a broken order; possible rival-student alliance against something worse.

brooks_alignment.part_1_setup: Chs 1-9 (~24%). Coruscant + Tarn Velos. Elya Rane's discovery and murder by Aevyn opens the central mystery; Ben recovers the damaged Jacen-encrypted manifest fragment; Ben tries the legal route to reach Talon Veyr in prison and is forced into a rescue when Greyline arrives. The Lie (Ben's: the GAG year has been categorized away) is established and reinforced. Closes with Ben breaking cover at the storm-line escape.
brooks_alignment.inciting_incident: Ch 4 (~11%) 'Not Well' — Ben arrives too late at Elya's murder scene, senses Force-trauma, and recovers the damaged Jacen-sealed duplicate manifest fragment. The case becomes Ben's.
brooks_alignment.first_plot_point: Ch 9 (~24%) 'Storm Line' — Ben and Talon cross storm-exposed gantries and sea-wall while pursued. Ben broke cover, freed a convicted prisoner, generated a public crisis. The forced partnership with Talon is the door Ben cannot return through. Within the canonical 20-25% Brooks window.
brooks_alignment.part_2_response: Chs 10-15 (~25-39%). Coruscant. Ben and Talon become a real investigative pair: Iressa Vossk at Civitas Archive Systems reconstructs the manifest trail; the GAG quarantine archive yields enough to point at the Foundation. Greyline + Vara hit the archive; Iressa dies after Ben refuses the Jacen-shaped coercive move.
brooks_alignment.first_pinch_point: Chs 14-15 (~37-39%) 'Cleanup Team' / 'The Bad Way' — Greyline archive cleanup with Vara Senn as Force specialist. Vara/Ben short ugly lightsaber clash, then Vara takes Iressa hostage. Ben refuses the Jacen-shaped coercive move. Iressa dies actively denying Vara a clean copy and transmitting the two-part dying package. The antagonist shows organized lethality; restraint costs the first life.
brooks_alignment.midpoint: Ch 16 (~42%) 'No Good Version' — Iressa's transmission carries the documentary chain AND the identity-shaping revelation (the Vigil intends to use the holocron's Recognition and Holding with Aevyn's help). Ben holo-calls Luke, then Saba: both correct, both too slow. Ben pivots from investigator to active disruptor — going to Iresh themselves. Slightly early of canonical 50% but compounded with PP1 in the same chapter.
brooks_alignment.part_3_attack: Chs 17-30 (~45-79%). Coruscant + Iresh transit + Iresh. Ben goes on offense: visits the Foundation and meets Aelia (social defeat); Talon spots Korda; Talon's manifest-correction bait surfaces Korda; chase leads to Iresh evidence. PP2 Squeeze closes every door. Off-grid transit. Iresh arrival, Sela alliance, Tavi seeded, Aevyn confronted, the cache discovered.
brooks_alignment.second_pinch_point: Ch 20 (~53%) 'Containment' — THE SQUEEZE. Three-part compounding pressure within hours: (1) Tess kills Korda as public fall guy and orders Iresh acceleration because Skywalker and Veyr are now involved; (2) Iressa's secondary cache is professionally raided and burned — the documentary case for Saba is unrecoverable, breach point unidentified; (3) Talon is framed for a current Coruscant crime with Tess's tradecraft fingerprint. Documentary path closed, legal cover destroyed, timeline destroyed. Relocation to the Skywalker apartment as final refuge. Slightly early of canonical 62-75% but compounds with PP1+Midpoint to deliver maximum pressure into Act 3's run-up.
brooks_alignment.second_plot_point: Ch 29 (~76%) 'The Cache Site' — at the Glasswell, Ben confirms what Iressa told them at the Midpoint — the holocron's unfinished Recognition and Holding work, Aevyn's presence as surviving student, the Vigil's intent. EMBODIMENT not revelation: the known threat becomes concrete. Only options left are rescue and denial. Within the canonical window.
brooks_alignment.part_4_resolution: Chs 31-38 (~82-100%). The Glasswell. Climax + flood + Iresh aftermath + Coruscant coda. Ben uses Jacen-shaped crisis logic to save Tavi and locals; defeats Aevyn in the consolidated duel; secures the unfinished holocron. Aelia steps down. Korda is the dead fall guy. Luke senses Ben's incomplete answer. Tess survives. White-blue spark in the dark.
brooks_alignment.climax: Chs 31-32 (~82-84%) 'Too Slow' / 'What He Left' — Ch 31 rescue first (Ben saves Tavi, Sela's locals, others through Jacen-shaped crisis logic; Aevyn recognizes the pattern); Ch 32 duel second (consolidated lightsaber duel across the collapsing Glasswell, two students of Jacen arguing through action). Ben wins by refusing to let Jacen own what he does with the lessons. The climax functions as ONE sustained beat rather than two.

structural_notes._scene_count_discipline: 38 chapters total. Most chapters carry ONE load-bearing scene. Multi-scene split-POV chapters (Ch 7, 9, 14-15, 16, 20, 33) earn the split because each scene carries a distinct turning point, mission, and emotional arc. Locked humanizing beats (Ch 2, 6, 11, 12, 17, 24, 28, 34) are woven into existing chapters as scene-level character texture, NOT separate scenes or chapters. Chapter Outlines v4.1 preserves the v4.0 consolidation of 9 chapter pairs from v3.3's 47-chapter draft — see continuity_note fields per consolidated chapter.
structural_notes._consolidation_history: v4.0 consolidations from v3.3 (47 -> 38 chapters): old Ch 1+2 -> new Ch 1 (Elya hook); old Ch 7+8 -> new Ch 6 (prison arrival + visitor room); old Ch 9+10 -> new Ch 7 (Greyline attack + Ben break-cover); old Ch 12 (Rusk POV) dropped; old Ch 17+18 -> new Ch 13 (reconstruction + archive entry); old Ch 23+24 -> new Ch 18 (Korda spotted + trap set); old Ch 25+26 -> new Ch 19 (chase + capture); old Ch 31+32 -> new Ch 24 (Iresh arrival + Sela refuses); old Ch 40+41 -> new Ch 32 (duel + victory as continuous climax). FPP shifted from 30% to 24% by the consolidation, landing inside the canonical Brooks 20-25% window.
structural_notes._act_structure: Three-act + coda. Act 1 Chs 1-10 (murder, clue, legal approach, prison break, Ben/Talon partnership forced into being); Act 2 Chs 11-23 (Coruscant investigation, Iressa death, Foundation/Vigil reveal, Korda/Tess escalation, Iresh lead); Act 3 Chs 24-34 (Iresh expedition, Sela/Tavi stakes, Aevyn, Glasswell collapse, duel, holocron recovered); Coda Chs 35-38 (public containment, Ben's morally incomplete holocron choice, One Sith adjustment, Aevyn survival hint).

terminology_registry.definition: Protagonist. Jedi Knight, age ~21 in 47 ABY. Son of Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade Skywalker. Briefly apprenticed to Jacen Solo as a fourteen-year-old; served in the Galactic Alliance Guard under Jacen; turned against Caedus by the end of the war. Lost Mara to Jacen/Caedus. Categorized by family as victim, by Order as survivor; neither category fully honest.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Talon calls him 'Skywalker' when guarded, 'Ben' when trust slips through. Sela calls him 'Skywalker' through Ch 28, then 'Ben' from Ch 34 onward. Aevyn calls him 'Ben Skywalker' — full name, never shortened — because the full name is the wound.

terminology_registry.definition: Co-protagonist / partner. 28, human, Coruscanti. Former GAG field agent turned black-channel logistics/security officer; imprisoned at Tarn Velos at story start. Was Colonel Maro Tess's protégé until Operation Glasshook; was reassigned into logistics/records after disobeying Tess to save trapped civilians. The reassignment became the record that ruined him.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Tess calls him 'Talon' — first name — with proprietary calm; Talon hates it. Korda's 'Veyr. I assumed they had better locks.' is the only line where Korda uses his surname.

terminology_registry.definition: True mirror antagonist. 28, human. Jacen Solo's surviving Force student from the GAG/Caedus period. Marginal Force-sensitive politely rejected by the Jedi at fourteen at a regional outreach office; later joined GAG as a young adult as a field analyst / operations specialist before the Caedus period; Jacen found him there and treated him as a side project while Ben remained the primary fourteen-year-old apprentice. Wields a self-built unstable cold white-blue lightsaber.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Aevyn refuses to call Jacen 'Caedus' — uses 'Jacen' only. The corridor flashback wound-image (Jacen leaving a session with Aevyn to walk off with young Ben) surfaces as fragment in his Act 3 POV — NEVER as exposition or speech. Aevyn presumed dead at Glasswell collapse; cold white-blue spark in Ch 38 confirms survival to the reader only.

terminology_registry.definition: Operational antagonist. Late forties, ~49. Former senior GAG operations officer; current Greyline Strategic Services strategist; operational architect for the Vigil; knowing One Sith asset. Was Talon Veyr's senior commander and mentor figure during the war; reassigned Talon out of field duty after Operation Glasshook. Believes power is real, hesitation kills, and morality is usually written after control has been secured.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Survives Book 1 and retreats deeper into One Sith service in Ch 37. NO villain poetry — Tess speaks operationally, like a man who sorts lives into categories. Treats failures as logistics.

terminology_registry.definition: Public-face antagonist. Late fifties, human. Executive Director of the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation. Former Senate staffer and widow from the Second Galactic Civil War. Warm, polished, prepared, genuinely compassionate, dangerous because much of what she says is true. Writes condolence notes by hand; remembers scholarship recipients' names; never publicly defends 'Darth Caedus'. Steps down in public disgrace in Ch 35 to preserve the Foundation's legitimate charitable work; no criminal liability.

terminology_registry.definition: Foundation security director. Early forties, human. Old GAG security lieutenant in respectable clothing. Talon knew him during GAG and disliked him.
terminology_registry.usage_notes: Killed/discarded by Tess in PP2 (Ch 20) as the public fall guy for the conspiracy's exposed crimes. Smooth with superiors, cruel through process, never openly messy when witnesses matter.

terminology_registry.definition: Galactic Alliance capital world. Anchors Acts 1-2 of the novel. The Jedi Order has NO institutional foothold here in 47 ABY — the Coruscant Jedi Temple was relinquished at the end of FOTJ (44 ABY) after the Senate voted to remove the Order following the Lost Tribe crisis. The Skywalker family apartment is the last Skywalker presence on a world that pushed the Order out.

Remote wind-scoured world near the edge of known space. Anchors Act 3. Pale mineral cliffs; cold highlands; dark water; black reed marshes; thin forests; long winds; wind-carved stone arches; shallow mirror-lakes; stacked stone path-markers; metal chimes / wind markers; thin aurora-like veils in the sky. Iresh's Force character: preserves charged impressions of memory, identity, and decision under pressure. Does NOT reveal truth or prophecy.

Every Act 3 chapter must include at least one grounding anchor (weather / terrain / local custom / physical danger / Sela's practical knowledge / Tavi's human stake / clear spatial geography). The Force atmosphere rides on top of that, not in place of it.

terminology_registry.definition: Taboo cavern/sinkhole system on Iresh, located beneath a mirror-lake and lined with pale translucent mineral that holds pressure-impressions unusually well. The cache hiding Jacen Solo's unfinished holocron is concealed near the Glasswell in old offworld survey equipment or a GAG-era storage unit — practical, deniable, Jacen-like. Local phrase: 'Some places remember too loudly.'

The cavern's geography MUST be physically clear before it collapses in Ch 30-32 (mirror-lake above; sinkhole below; pale mineral walls; survey scaffold; cache embedded in survey/GAG equipment; lower ledge where Tavi is trapped; one main path out; one dangerous water route).
